## Diagnosis
The remaining headroom is only for `assortment_problem` in this DEEPEN step. The previous layer added a strong helper for the single-segment MNL assortment model, including optional cardinality constraints. That helps when the benchmark is exactly the classic MNL revenue problem, but assortment benchmarks often use richer structures: multiple customer classes/segments, scenario weights, per-segment attraction matrices, or a cardinality/budget cap. In those cases, the single-segment threshold characterization is no longer exact, and blindly applying it can under-score because the optimal assortment must trade off cannibalization across segments.

## Intervention
Add a second reusable helper, `segmented_mnl_assortment`, targeting `assortment_problem` instances where the data resembles multi-segment MNL / scenario-weighted assortment optimization. It computes the true segmented expected revenue, builds multiple robust starting assortments, then runs add/drop/swap local search under optional cardinality/budget constraints. This is the kind of objective-specific local search the solver may not reliably implement from scratch under time pressure, especially because the objective is fractional and segment-coupled.

## Why this is different
The prior intervention only covered the exact single-segment MNL threshold rule. This layer adds a structurally different algorithm for multi-segment assortment, where no simple revenue threshold is globally optimal. It preserves the previous helper for its correct regime and supplies a more general objective evaluator/local-search optimizer for the likely regression/headroom regime.
